hints: Look at what propanoic acid is reacting with in each case, an alkali, a metal, a carbonate, or a base, and recall the general products for that type.
Remember that acid plus metal carbonate always makes three things, a salt plus carbon dioxide plus water.
Compare each set of products shown to that expected list and spot which one is missing a product.
walkthrough:
**Recall the four acid patterns**

Carboxylic acids behave like other acids when forming salts. Keep these patterns in mind.

$$\text{acid + alkali} \rightarrow \text{salt + water}$$
$$\text{acid + metal} \rightarrow \text{salt + hydrogen}$$
$$\text{acid + carbonate} \rightarrow \text{salt + carbon dioxide + water}$$

**Check A, B and D**

Reaction A with $\text{KOH}$ gives potassium propanoate plus $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. That fits acid plus alkali.

Reaction B with $\text{Mg}(s)$ gives magnesium propanoate plus $\text{H}_2(g)$. That fits acid plus metal, and two $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ ions balance one $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

Reaction D with $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ gives calcium propanoate plus $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$. That fits acid plus base, and again two propanoate ions balance one $\text{Ca}^{2+}$.

**Spot the incomplete reaction**

Reaction C with $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ should give sodium propanoate plus $\text{CO}_2(g)$ plus $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$.

Only the salt and $\text{CO}_2$ are shown, so water is missing. This is the one that does not show all the correct products.

options.A: Incorrect. Propanoic acid plus KOH is a neutralisation: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-\text{K}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Both products shown are correct and complete.
options.B: Incorrect. Propanoic acid plus magnesium is acid plus reactive metal: salt plus hydrogen. The formula $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-)_2\text{Mg}^{2+}$ correctly balances the 2+ charge, and $\text{H}_2(g)$ is correct.
options.C: Correct. Acid plus carbonate must give salt plus carbon dioxide plus water. The equation should be $2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Water is missing, so not all correct products are shown.
options.D: Incorrect. Propanoic acid plus $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ is acid plus base: salt plus water. The formula $(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-)_2\text{Ca}^{2+}$ correctly balances the 2+ charge, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)$ is correct.
